## Credit and provenance

The **Edit key family structure** dialog is based on the contribution by
**Karna Mandarawata ([karna-stats](https://github.com/karna-stats))** in
[NADABAS PR #41](https://github.com/statisticsnorway/nadabas/pull/41), commit
`60e43df42425552771a3ae37411fef8d85677d69`.

The original binary dialog designer, `dlgEditKeyFamily.frx`, is retained
unchanged. The dimension reordering code is adapted from that contribution.
The dialog code has been adapted to stage changes and use the existing PR #38
schema application workflow, with the empty-only safeguards described below.
Credit is also recorded in the VBA source and the 6.02.005 release notes.

Suggested release acknowledgement:

> Thanks to Karna Mandarawata (@karna-stats) for the Edit key family structure
> dialog in PR #41. Version 6.02.005 selectively adapts this contribution to
> allow structure editing only for empty key families.

For the integration commit, retain your own authorship and add this trailer
(the name and address come from the original public commit):

```text
Co-authored-by: Karna Mandarawata <karna.mandarawata@asean.org>
```

## What was taken into 6.02.005

| File | Integration |
|---|---|
| `vba/forms/dlgEditKeyFamily.frx` | Original PR #41 designer, unchanged. |
| `vba/forms/dlgEditKeyFamily.frm` | Adapted dialog, staged dimension edits and reordering; attributed to Karna. |
| `vba/forms/frmKeyFamily.frm` | Original Key families layout with only an Edit structure button and empty-only availability. |
| `vba/modules/KeyFamilyEditPolicy.bas` | New live row check and exclusive Access connection helper. |
| `vba/modules/KeyFamilyMigration.bas` | Existing schema workflow with backend checks, locking and rollback. |
| `vba/resources/office-ui.csv` | Four-language caption for the manager's new button. |

The new editor itself uses English captions. The existing translated controls
and the earlier 6.02.005 save-conflict improvements remain in place.

The PR's custom error dialog, post-creation prompt, unrelated class/module
changes, whole-key-family rename, populated-table migration and shared
dimension-length modifications have not been imported. The rename control
edits a selected dimension in the local draft only.

## How to reproduce the selective import

These commands describe the **starting point on a clean integration branch**.
Do not run the restore command over the already adapted 6.02.005 files, because
that would replace the safeguards with the upstream dialog code.

```powershell
git fetch origin pull/41/head:refs/remotes/review/pr41
git show --no-patch --format=fuller review/pr41
git diff HEAD...review/pr41 -- vba/forms/dlgEditKeyFamily.frm
git restore --source=60e43df42425552771a3ae37411fef8d85677d69 -- vba/forms/dlgEditKeyFamily.frm vba/forms/dlgEditKeyFamily.frx
```

Then apply the adaptations listed above, their regression tests, and the
release documentation. Import both the `.frm` and its `.frx` when introducing
the form into Excel; existing manager forms need their code updated while
preserving their designers. Use this repository's VBA import tooling and
apply the language resources to both the XLAM and XLSM.

Do not cherry-pick the whole upstream commit: it combines this feature with
other changes that are outside the requested scope. The current working tree
already contains the adapted implementation; a reviewer can compare it with
the pinned upstream commit without repeating the import.

## Empty-only behavior

An administrator can edit a selected key family only when a live query finds
**zero rows**. A row with a NULL Value still counts as data. Other key families
in the database may contain data. Missing tables, unsupported databases and
query/connection failures disable editing.

The manager checks availability, the dialog checks again on entry, and the
backend checks again before applying. The main window preserves its original
layout and maintenance buttons; the extra inline draft and workbook-migration
buttons have been removed at the user's request. Editing the draft does not change the database;
Apply requires confirmation. Cancel discards the draft.

For Access (MDB/ACCDB), Apply temporarily reopens the connection with exclusive
database access. Another open connection prevents the change. After acquiring
exclusive access the row count is checked again. The normal connection mode
is restored after success or failure; a restoration failure asks the operator
to reopen the database. This is a short exclusive-access requirement, not a
requirement that the entire database be empty.

This stronger Access boundary was added after a disposable ACE test showed
that a concurrent asynchronous insert could remain invisible even after a
transactional rename. Jet/ACE buffering is why a SELECT-only check is not
sufficient; Microsoft documents the related asynchronous commit and cache
properties in its [Jet provider reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/client-developer/access/desktop-database-reference/microsoft-ole-db-provider-for-microsoft-jet).

SQL Server uses `TABLOCKX, HOLDLOCK` in the transaction. Its runtime integration
still needs verification on a disposable SQL Server database.

The Access check uses plain `adModeShareExclusive` (12). In the installed ACE
provider, combining this with the read/write flags reported mode 15 but retained
shared access. The Windows regression script tests actual cross-process denial,
not just the reported mode, and preserves its disposable fixture and results.

The replacement and retained recovery table are handled in a transaction.
A final check of the original table occurs after its rename and before commit.
No existing rows are copied or deleted by this feature. Workbook definitions
remain a separate explicit workflow, as in PR #38.

## Final Excel checklist

1. Compile each candidate using Debug > Compile NADABAS and confirm 6.02.005.
2. As administrator, select an empty family in a database containing another
   populated family: Edit structure should be available.
3. Select a family with one row, including a NULL Value: Edit structure should
   be disabled. Repeat as a non-administrator and with a failed connection.
4. Test add, remove, rename, length and order changes; Cancel must leave the
   schema unchanged. Apply must change only the selected empty family.
5. Insert and commit a row from another connection after opening the dialog:
   Apply must refuse to change the schema.
6. For Access, keep another connection open: Apply must fail without schema
   changes and restore ordinary use. Close the other connection and retry.
7. Check that another populated family's schema and rows remain unchanged,
   and verify the prior save-conflict choices.

Use disposable database copies. The supplied 6.02.004 Office files have been
preserved; the new candidates are unsigned test builds.
